newsitem.title: UK: UK Q2 NEW CONSTRUCTION ORDERS HIGHEST SINCE END-95.
newsitem.headline: UK Q2 NEW CONSTRUCTION ORDERS HIGHEST SINCE END-95.

text.p: The total volume of new construction orders received by contractors in Britain in the three months to June rose a seasonally adjusted five percent from the previous three months to its highest level since the end of 1995, the Department of Environment said on Thursday.
New orders were eight percent up on the same three months a year ago. In current prices the total value of new orders in June alone was 2.01 billion stg.
The rise over the latest three months was mainly due to large increases in the infrastructure, public non-housing and private industrial sectors.

New orders in the private housing sector in the three months to June were four percent lower compared with the previous three months but nine percent higher than in the corresponding period a year ago.
Public housing and housing association orders in the latest three months were 18 percent lower than in the previous three months and nine percent lower than a year earlier.
Infrastructure orders in the latest three months were 33 percent higher compared with the previous three months and seven percent higher than a year ago.

Public non-housing orders (excluding infrastructure) in the latest three months were 14 percent higher compared with the previous three months but three percent lower than in the corresponding period a year ago.

Private industrial orders in the latest three months were nine percent higher than in the previous three months and 37 percent higher than a year ago. Private commercial orders in the latest three months were three percent lower compared with the previous three months but six percent higher than in the corresponding period a year earlier.
